I am a woman of 44 years in the North East of Nigeria, farming beans on land I rent, so I must be careful with money. The rains here are not always kind, and fertilizer prices have gone up too much, so I will use only a small amount of urea and rely on the manure I gather from my goats and neighbor's cattle. I plant my own seeds I kept from last harvest, intercropped with sorghum to protect the soil and give my family more food. For pests like the pod borers I will spray a little when I see them eating the pods, but I cannot afford to irrigate — I depend on the rain like my mother did.
